answer: Make the writing itself the bond: each identity signs with a distinct quill, a public key, and stakes collateral shared by its funding ancestry. When linked accounts submit near-identical wording in one epoch, the ledger strips the plume from both, slashing standing and bonded balance to the reporter, and sets a sable mark on that ancestry, a permanent flag barring re-entry. A farm must buy a separate quill and collateral per head, and every extra clone raises the chance its siblings trip the correlation check. Cost grows faster than head count, and a burned cluster cannot rebrand.
